item.description: tests: fix CI flakes of TOPK_MOE caused by near ties (#31426) * tests: fix CI flakes of TOPK_MOE caused by near ties With uniform random logits, two experts sometimes land within one f32 ulp of each other at a routing boundary, mostly with sqrt_softplus gating whose output range is narrow. A backend whose gating differs by a few ulps from the CPU then picks the other expert and the test fails. Draw each row of logits again until the group selection and the final top-k both have a relative margin of 1e-4, computed on the host in double precision. * tests: build the TOPK_MOE logits by inverting the gating function Draw the selection scores (probs plus bias) of each row as a random permutation of a grid, move the experts of the best groups up by half a step, and set the logits to the inverse of the gating function at these scores. Every expert and group decision is then one grid step apart on all backends, and the host no longer recomputes the routing. The softmax probs are built to sum to one so that the softmax keeps the scores, and the views of the logits are not initialized again after the logits are set. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: ## Overview This release adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization support, a new flash_attn_ext_rows op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. Four new architectures are supported (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4), audio generation and transcription expand with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, and the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models get major prefill optimizations. ggml is updated to v0.29.0, bringing FP8 E4M3, flash attention rows, NCCL-based multi-node tensor parallelism and performance work across the CPU, CUDA, SYCL, Metal, Vulkan, OpenCL and Hexagon backends. The server and UI receive a round of fixes and refinements. ### Highlights - Quant: OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type (saturating mode) with conversion helpers and a new ftype (#27512) - llama: flash_attn_ext_rows - more efficient unified KV for multi-seq, restoring non-unified KV prefill performance (#29510) - ggml: batched tensor copy API (ggml_backend_tensor_copy_n/set_n/get_n) superseding the _2d API, implemented for Metal and CUDA (#30881) - For a 3rd year in a row, llama.cpp is a featured repo in the Github Octoverse report: ### API changes - llama.h: add LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_F8_E4M3 (#27512) - mtmd.h: add MTMD_GEN_AUDIO_TYPE_CHATTERBOX and n_voices to mtmd_gen_audio_info (#30993) - mtmd.h: add predefined-voice APIs: mtmd_gen_audio_voice_name(), mtmd_gen_audio_get_voice(), mtmd_gen_state_set_ref() (#30993) - mtmd.h: add mtmd_bitmap_is_voice() and mtmd_gen_audio_read_tensor() (#30993) - mtmd.h: add MTMD_VIDEO_TEMPLATE_QWEN3VL video prompt template (#31619) - server: GET /props reports the model's predefined TTS voices; the TTS endpoint accepts predefined voice names (#30993) - server: /v1/responses now merges extra_params (seed, min_p, ...) into the converted chat-completions response (#30959) ### New models - Clover-35B-A3B-Preview diffusion model, AR mode (#31306) - Limite 1B - Violetto (#29433) - Metis-1.6 (Praxis ~2.9B and Logos ~10.2B): hybrid Mamba-2 / GQA attention with fixed-depth recurrence and LatentMoE (#31134) - Mistral Large 4 (#31376) ### Core changes - gemma4: graph optimizations with massive prefill gains for E2B and E4B (#31356); create token_embd before the tied output in gemma3n and gemma4 (#31394) - LFM3: enable NVFP4 GGUFs (#31608), enable tensor split (#31431), quantize the audio codec decoder (#31386) - spec dec: save and restore MTP hidden state in context checkpoints (#30141) and record LFM3 layer inputs (#31598) - dflash: copy hidden features via device copies (#31506); qwen4exp: write the conv state tail without an intermediate cont (#31443) - model loading: reuse the tensor staging buffer and skip the direct-IO bounce buffer (#31321) - kv-cache: keep Hadamard rotation constants on the GPU (#31073) and fix attention tensor rotation in layers with shared KV (#31406) - kv-cache: never return 0 kv_rows for sequences without cells (#31570) and refuse rollbacks past the snapshots of the last ubatch (#31368) - Gemma4 MTP assistant: follow ctx_other devices and flash-attention setting (#31635); DSV4: remove simple batch splitting (#31300) - chat: strip the qwen3-coder think block with reasoning_format none (#31380) and end reasoning budget forcing on a prompt end tag (#31374) - chat: allow a constraint type after the gpt-oss final channel (#31556); common: fix -hf tag matching inside longer quant names (#31620) and bound control vector layer indices (#31336) - tools: reject mismatched shards in GGUF split merge (#31579), fix imatrix --nextn crash (#31522), fix gguf-py np_roundf dropping the sign (#31310) - vendor: miniaudio 0.11.26 (#31459) and cpp-httplib 0.64.0 (#31400); embed an app manifest in all Windows executables (#31329) ### Multi-modality changes - add Chatterbox TTS support (#30993) - add Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe support: offline transcription in 40 languages with prompt context and speaker attribution (#31471) - Pocket TTS: support predefined voices without voice cloning (#31429) - accurate support for the qwen3-vl video prompt format (#31619) - resize Gemma 4 images without letterbox padding (#30922) and fix InternVL CLS token order (#30886) ### Server changes - cap shared decision prefixes at the first output (#30710) - restore the speculative checkpoint for drafts longer than n_rs_seq (#31350) ### UI changes - add MCP group checkboxes in the tools settings (#31303) and request persistent storage on startup (#31299) - keep chats at the bottom until the reader scrolls up (#31311) and show the submit button when the input has content (#31324) - reveal the collapsed sidebar from its logo (#31307) and align alert dialog styling (#31312) - keep queued steering messages in their own conversation (#31304) and show an interrupted state for tool calls that never returned (#31314) - disable model deletion the server would refuse (#31305) and prefer a loading model in pre-selection (#31326) - add a Playwright harness for recording demo videos (#31318) and run local browser tests in installed Chrome (#31596) ### ggml changes - v0.29.0: ggml v0.29.0 adds an OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type, a new ggml_flash_attn_ext_rows op where each query slice attends to its own list of K/V rows, a batched tensor copy API, and initial support for multi-node tensor parallelism through a new multi-process communicator interface. Core improvements include bounding tensor views by the bytes their strides reach, zero-copy GGUF export of host-buffer tensors, and vm_allocate-based allocations on Apple platforms. Performance work spans all major backends: new SVE kernels in the CPU backend, DPAS flash attention for quantized KV in SYCL, fused MoE MMQ in CUDA, faster MXFP4 mat-vec in Metal, split-K tuning in Vulkan, and a large expansion of quantized GEMM/GEMV coverage in OpenCL. The Hexagon backend gains support for several new ops, including the lightning indexer, top-k mask, conv2d and upscale. ## Assets **Nightly build:** b12110 ## More info - Releases and versioning of item.description: ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach (#31584) * ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach A view was checked against its source with the size of a contiguous tensor of the same shape, computed before its strides were set. Views whose rows overlap failed that check although they stay inside their source, and views with wider strides passed it while reaching past the end. The view functions now pass their strides to the tensor constructor, which checks the bytes they actually reach, like ggml_nbytes. The conv windows of delta_net are created with all their rows at once instead of being widened after the check. * ggml: assert that a strided view starts from contiguous elements The view functions set nb[0] to the type size, so the source must have contiguous elements along dim 0 for the view to read them. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: vulkan: fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup (#31079) * vulkan : fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup On the non-OCP path, ue4m3_fp32_lut has 128 entries and is indexed with the raw scale byte. ggml_validate_row_data accepts every byte and ggml_ue4m3_to_fp32 ignores bit 7, so a byte >= 0x80 reads past the shared array. Vulkan robustness does not cover shared memory. Size the table, both init loops, and the two host shared-memory budgets to 256 entries. ue4m3_to_fp32_build() already masks the exponent and treats only 0 and 0x7F as special, so entries 128-255 match the CPU. A 256-entry table keeps 0xFF distinct from 0x7F: the CPU decodes 0xFF as a non-zero value and 0x7F as zero. Each NVFP4 pipeline uses 512 more bytes of shared memory. ggml_fp32_to_ue4m3 never sets bit 7, so models quantized by llama.cpp are unaffected. item.description: hexagon: tiled hvx permute (#31446) * hexagon: add tiled HVX transpose path for permuted CONT/CPY Permuted copies where dst dim 0 is strided in src, but some other src dim is contiguous, used to fall back to HTP_COPY_KERNEL_RESHAPE. That issues one DMA descriptor per element. The channel-first <-> channel-last permutes around per-channel norms (e.g. [W,H,T,C] <-> [C,W,H,T] in video VAEs) ht this path, and these copies ran at about 45 MB/s. Add HTP_COPY_KERNEL_TRANSPOSE for same-type, same-shape f32/f16 copies into a contiguous dst. Host: - drop extent-1 dims and merge dims that stay adjacent in src into a canonical view, stored in the kernel params. There are no minimum size limits. - the copy is treated as a 2D transpose between dst dim 0 and the contiguous src dim, batched over the remaining dims. - tiles are sized to 64 KB per buffer and halved until they fit in session VTCM. blkk is capped so the halfword vgather offsets fit in 16 bits. Kernel, per tile: - 2D DMA of blk0 strided src rows (blkk contiguous elements each) into VTCM - vgather transpose in 32x32 (f32) or 64x64 (f16) blocks - 2D DMA of blkk contiguous rows out to dst Staged and transposed buffers are double-buffered, so the next tile's input DMA overlaps the current transpose and output DMA. Tiles are split across threads and mdev sessions. Small dims: - packed mode: when dim k follows dim 0 and dim 0 divides the HVX lanes (f32: 2/4/8/16, f16: 2/4/.../32), one vgather writes several whole dst rows, and each tile goes out as one contiguous DMA. - when the contiguous src dim fits in one vector, it is staged exactly and the tile is made long along dim 0. All other copies select the same kernels as before. Tests: add test_cont cases for perms {1,2,3,0} and {3,0,1,2}, f32 and f16, at various sizes. * hexagon: cpy transpose cleanups - fix vgather halfword offset comments: offsets are unsigned 16-bit, caps are kept lower for speed - set packed directly in the packed case - add dim_k == 3 CONT tests (full reversal) Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 * hexagon: use cpy transpose path for ne[0] == 1 permutes - drop the nb[0] check in the transpose solver: size-1 dims are skipped, and the canonical tp.nb[0] check covers packed dim 0 - try the transpose path before SAMESHAPE_SAMETYPE, which did one DMA per element for these - add ne[0] == 1 permute CPY tests Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 * hex-cpy: further improve cpy Bring in improvements from aizip branch/PR. Cleanup kparams and replace divs with fastdiv. Co-authored-by: Yiwei Shao * hex-cpy: avoid vtcm bank conflicts * hex-cpy: trim down the comments * cpy-test: trim down new tests that cover permute scenarios --------- Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky Co-authored-by: Yiwei Shao **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: mtmd: Pocket tts - support for voices without voice cloning (#31429) * feat: support PocketTTS voices with no voice cloning The kyutai/pocket-tts-without-voice-cloning weights ship predefined voices as the backbone KV state after the voice prompt. The converter turns each state back into the prompt embeddings and stores them in the mmproj (voice. ), the zeroed voice encoder is left out, and the "voice" field of /tts and --tts-voice select one of them. A speaker reference is rejected when the model has no voice encoder. Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1 * convert : pocket-tts voices never fail the conversion, log the drift of the state The voice states shipped by Kyutai are not always the ones the pack's weights give for the prompt: italian, german and spanish match within the bf16 rounding, english_2026-04 is 2% off and french 20% (its layer 0 state comes from other weights), while the reference loads them as is and they still sound like the same voice. The converter now re-prompts the backbone with the recovered embeddings, compares the whole state and logs the distance per voice, warning above 5%. A state that does not belong to the weights at all is skipped, so the packs of kyutai/pocket-tts convert too. Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1 * mtmd : list the predefined voices, expose them in GET /props mtmd_gen_audio_info gains n_voices and mtmd_gen_audio_voice_name() the names, with the voices worded as a feature of any audio generation model. The server lists them under "voices" in /props when the model ships some. Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1 * server : an unknown voice is a bad request A model with predefined voices answers 400 naming the voice instead of 500 "failed to process TTS prompt". A model without them ignores "voice" with a warning, as the other audio generation models do. Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1 * refactor api * fix conversion * small renaming * fix lint * tts : a model with predefined voices speaks with the first one by default Without a voice prompt such a model only produces near silence. When neither a voice nor a speaker reference is given, llama-tts and the server now take the first predefined voice and say so in the log, as the LFM3-Audio template does with its default voice. Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1 * mtmd : one comment per voice accessor, converter states the rule only The clip.h comment described clip_gen_get_voice but sat above all three functions; the converter comment quoted the drift measured per pack, which goes stale with the next upload of the weights. Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1 * clean up redundant code and comments * mtmd: match the LFM3-Audio voice name case-insensitively The tts chat template lowers the voice name, so Male speaks with the male voice; the voice lookup lowers it the same way and names the bitmap after the canonical voice. --------- Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: sycl : vectorize reordered-layout dequantization stores (Q4_0, K-quants, IQ3, MXFP4) (#30976) * sycl : widen reordered q4_0 dequantization stores The reordered-layout Q4_0 conversion kernel processed one qs byte per work-item with two scalar stores, strided 16 elements apart. Give it the same treatment the Q8_0 kernel got in #30775: a flat sycl::range<1> launch with four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec stores. Same float math and rounding as the scalar kernel; output is bit-identical. The existing k % QK4_0 == 0 assert guarantees whole 32-element blocks, so the k/8 launch covers every row exactly. The now-unreferenced scalar reorder kernel is removed. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a reorder-installed tensor): +6.4% to +7.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_0 models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill and decode unchanged; PPL within run noise. * sycl : vectorize reordered q4_K dequantization stores The reordered-layout Q4_K conversion kernel already loads its quantized inputs through sycl::vec but writes the dequantized results with scalar stores. Build the results in a vec register and emit two vector stores instead. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a reorder-installed tensor): +14.7% to +15.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_K-dominant models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : remap reordered q5_K dequantization to vec4 loads/stores The reordered-layout Q5_K conversion kernel gave each thread only four outputs fed by scalar ql/qh byte loads plus a local-memory scale broadcast, so the stores were never its bottleneck: widening the stores alone measured within noise on mixed-quant models and +0.5% on a q5_K-dominant model. Re-decompose to 32 threads per block, each consuming four consecutive ql and qh bytes and emitting two aligned vec stores; a 4-element run shares one scale pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill on a q5_K-dominant 27B model: +3.6% pp512/pp2048 over the scalar kernel; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. The GET_ROWS reorder path moves to the same 32-thread decomposition. * sycl : remap reordered q6_K dequantization to vec4 stores The reordered-layout Q6_K conversion kernel wrote four scalars per thread, strided 32 elements apart, each pair of neighbors sharing neither instruction stream nor store transaction. Re-decompose the same 64-thread work-group so each thread emits one aligned vec : a 4-element run shares one 16-element scale group, one ql nibble source and one qh bit pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical to the scalar kernel. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +28.7% pp512/pp2048 on a Q6_K 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : vectorize reordered q3_K dequantization stores Each thread of the reordered-layout Q3_K conversion kernel already computes four consecutive outputs; build them in a vec register and emit one vector store instead of four scalars. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +16.8% pp512/pp2048 on a Q3_K-dominant 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : vectorize reordered iq3_xxs/iq3_s dequantization stores Both reordered-layout IQ3 conversion kernels write eight contiguous outputs per thread as scalar stores (four from each grid lookup). Build two vec registers and emit two vector stores. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +20.3% to +21.1% pp512/pp2048 on IQ3_XXS- and IQ3_S-dominant 27B models; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : remap reordered q2_K dequantization to vec4 stores Re-decompose the reordered-layout Q2_K conversion kernel the same way as Q6_K: one aligned vec per thread instead of four scalars strided 32 apart. A 4-element run shares one scale byte and one 2-bit lane, so the per-element math and the output are identical to the scalar kernel. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +13.1% pp512/pp2048 on a Q2_K-dominant 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : widen reordered mxfp4 dequantization stores Give the reordered-layout MXFP4 conversion kernel the same flat sycl::range<1> launch as Q4_0: four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec stores. Same LUT lookups and per-block scale; output is bit-identical. The k % QK_MXFP4 == 0 assert guarantees whole blocks, so the k/8 launch covers every row exactly. The old scalar kernel is removed. The reordered layout for MXFP4 is installed on the MoE expert path (reorder_qw_mxfp4_moe); dense MXFP4 tensors keep the normal layout. item.description: ggml-openvino: slice view inputs of SCALE (#31334) SCALE now accepts a src0 view with arbitrary row strides. translate_scale used the raw input, and on the dynamic path a VIEW translates to its whole source tensor, so a strided view input scaled the entire source. The model output then had the source's size, and copying it back overran the result buffer, which crashes test-backend-ops on the SCALE view cases. Slice the input with process_view_input_new, as the other translators do. A batch of new architectures landed: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, SenseNova U1, Beam, Kolibri-1, Flint, Muse Spark, Granite Switch Decision, plus decision/embedding models from LiquidAI, Baidu and NVIDIA.
